messages.speaker: Eli
messages.text: The synthetic sensor samples currently stay forever in the teaching archive. I propose deleting them after seven days.

messages.speaker: June
messages.text: Some lessons compare two weeks. Seven days breaks those exercises. Can we use a separate scratch bucket?

messages.speaker: Eli
messages.text: Agreed: retain the teaching archive unchanged. Put new disposable samples in scratch-demo with a proposed 21-day lifecycle.

messages.speaker: June
messages.text: I wrote lifecycle-draft-2.json. It targets scratch-demo only. I have not applied it.

messages.text: Dry-run report lr-2 lists 18 synthetic objects in scratch-demo. It lists zero objects in teaching-archive. That report does not delete anything.

messages.speaker: Eli
messages.text: Keep the lifecycle unapplied until I check the dry-run object list. June owns the draft; I own approval. No deletion is authorized by this chat.

Check the dry-run object list before considering approval.

messages.speaker: Noor
messages.text: Our invented workshop audio has three speakers. The transcript exporter labels all of them Speaker 1 after a pause. I can inspect the saved export today.

messages.speaker: Ben
messages.text: It may be the silence threshold. That is a guess, not a diagnosis.

messages.speaker: Noor
messages.text: Saved segment table seg-9 has three distinct speaker IDs after the pause. The text export txt-9 collapses those IDs. I have not rerun recognition.

messages.speaker: Ben
messages.text: Then let us edit the exporter mapping, not the recognizer threshold. I will prepare a patch.

messages.speaker: Ben
messages.text: Patch exp-4 preserves the IDs in the saved fixture. Its output text now has three labels. This is a fixture test only.

messages.speaker: Noor
messages.text: I accept the fixture result. Keep a full new audio run pending; I will schedule it after the microphone stand arrives. Delivery date is unknown.

items.text: seg-9 retains three speaker IDs after the pause, but txt-9 collapses them; recognition was not rerun.
The chosen fix is exporter mapping rather than changing the recognizer threshold.
exp-4 preserves three labels in the saved fixture, and Noor accepts that bounded result.
